html:
A port town on Sao Vicente island that grew from the 1850s as a coaling station for British steamships crossing the Atlantic, on the deep bay of Porto Grande.

Before it, Sao Vicente was nearly empty. British coal companies brought work, ships and news, and Mindelo became the most open and cosmopolitan town of the islands. It was the home of the literary magazine Claridade, founded in 1936, which began a Cape Verdean literature. When ships moved to oil, the coal trade declined from the 1920s and hunger and emigration followed. Mindelo stayed the centre of morna and carnival, and the home of Cesaria Evora. See also emigration.
